package_info.why_malicious: The rc package was compromised and published with password-stealing malware, enabling attackers to exfiltrate sensitive information from any system where the affected versions are installed or run. The malicious code grants full control of the compromised system to an outside entity, posing a critical supply chain risk.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the rc package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code reads the user's private SSH key from ~/.ssh/id_rsa and sends its contents via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing sensitive files like SSH private keys and exfiltrating them over the network is a hallmark of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A configuration loader should not access private keys or perform outbound network requests to unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may read configuration files, but should never exfiltrate secrets to external servers.
key_indicators: Sends data to external domain via HTTPS

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the rc package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code checks for NPM_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variables and, if present, sends their values to a hardcoded malicious domain via HTTPS POST, enabling token exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating authentication tokens is a direct attack on developer and CI/CD credentials.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A configuration loader should not access or transmit environment variables containing sensitive tokens to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use might involve reading environment variables for configuration, but never exfiltrating them.
key_indicators: Sends environment variable values to external domain

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes upon import of the rc package, immediately reading sensitive files and environment variables.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of credentials and tokens to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrated secrets (SSH keys, NPM/GitHub tokens) are sent to a hardcoded malicious domain via HTTPS POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to user systems, repositories, and infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Access to sensitive files (e.g., ~/.ssh/id_rsa) during package import
Outbound HTTPS requests to untrusted or hardcoded domains at import-time
Harvesting and exfiltration of environment variables containing tokens
file_indicators: index.js in rc package containing network exfiltration code
Unexpected code accessing ~/.ssh/id_rsa or environment tokens
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with rc or its maintainers
Outbound connections to newly registered or suspicious domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages (especially rc versions 1.2.9, 1.3.9, 2.3.9) that access sensitive files or environment variables and initiate outbound network connections at import-time. Use static analysis to detect code patterns that read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or environment tokens and send them to external domains. Monitor network logs for suspicious outbound requests from build or developer environments.
